clue.text: Loud turn, in reality

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an act or turn is one performer's spot on a variety bill

explanation.surface: A noisy stage act that turns out to be real, or a loud spin happening in actual life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here; reading 'in reality' as the definition fails, since the answer is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact is something actually true, so it stands for reality or truth as a synonym.

clue.text: Fine expert to take up cosmetic surgery?

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an ace is a highly skilled person
to lift is to take something up

explanation.surface: A skilled surgeon agreeing to take on cosmetic work, phrased as a job notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: this is one kind of cosmetic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is a common cosmetic operation tightening the skin of the face, so it exemplifies that surgery.

clue.text: Draughts in country house retreat

definitions.meaning: another name for the board game draughts (checkers in the US)
The British Prime Minister's official country house in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: Cold air blowing through a stately home used as a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draughts' reads as chilly gusts but means the board game; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game played on a chequered board shares its name with the Prime Minister's weekend residence.

clue.text: They may be on the dinner table also, with most of the choices

definitions.text: They may be on the dinner table

parts.note: too means also

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word before it is dropped

parts.note: the word 'the' itself
picks are choices, as in 'take your pick'

explanation.surface: Items set out on a dinner table alongside a selection of dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims 'the' to TH; 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Small wooden sticks for cleaning teeth are often set out in holders on restaurant tables.

clue.text: Man-eating monsters rose unsteadily after swallowing gallons

indicators.note: after swallowing says the scrambled rose takes the next piece into itself
unsteadily suggests the letters of rose wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: Fairy-tale beasts lurching to their feet after downing a vast quantity of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsteadily' turns ROSE into ORES, and 'after swallowing' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres in folk tales are giants who devour humans, hence man-eating monsters.

clue.text: Form of loyalty in bar limits changes

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of bar limits are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub's opening restrictions being altered, framed as a kind of allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' is the anagram signal for BAR LIMITS; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribalism is strong allegiance to one's own group, a particular kind of loyalty.

clue.text: Show, unavoidably, must involve staff

indicators.note: must involve says the first word takes the next one inside it

parts.note: perforce is an old word meaning by necessity, unavoidably
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A production that, like it or not, has to employ personnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is a verb here, to man, not a noun for employees or a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance is a show put on before an audience, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Play that of coronation anew

indicators.note: anew says the letters of that of coronation are made up afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A drama based on a royal crowning, staged a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anew' is the anagram signal for THAT OF CORONATION, sixteen letters giving the full title.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee Williams wrote this 1955 stage drama about a Southern family, so the title names a play.

clue.text: Fancy woman not having married, I repeat

indicators.note: not having says the following letters are taken away

parts.note: a fancy woman is a mistress

explanation.surface: A man insisting, again, that his lover is unmarried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' removes M and I from the start of MISTRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise it, much as one does by saying it again.

clue.text: One running the kitchen's hurt sacking a female

indicators.note: sacking means dismissing, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: A cook in pain after firing a woman from the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking a' drops A from ACHE, leaving CHE; 's (is) is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is the professional cook in charge of a restaurant's kitchen.

clue.text: Judge right to enter diabolical abattoir by river

indicators.note: by means next to, so the last piece is set alongside
to enter says the next piece goes into the jumbled letters
diabolical means dreadful or shambolic, signalling abattoir is jumbled

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A judge right at a dreadful slaughterhouse beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diabolical' turns ABATTOIR into ARBITATO; 'to enter' puts R inside it, and 'by' adds a final R.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbitrator settles disputes between parties, acting as a judge or referee.

clue.text: New rules do in place of pilgrimage

indicators.note: New tells us the letters of rules do form something new

explanation.surface: Fresh regulations brought in at a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lourdes in south-west France draws millions of Catholic pilgrims to its Marian shrine.

clue.text: Drink with father, fast one, in Ulster town

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
pa is an informal word for father
pulling a fast one means playing a trick

explanation.surface: A pint with Dad and a con trick in a Northern Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast one' is an idiom for a deception, not something quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Downpatrick in County Down, Northern Ireland, is traditionally the burial place of St Patrick.

clue.text: Numbers grow while outside

indicators.note: outside says the first word sits around the second

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as he spoke'
to mount is to grow or increase

explanation.surface: Figures rising while out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal, not an adverb about being outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Amounts are quantities or totals, which numbers also denote.

clue.text: Reportedly what King Harold did in Scottish town

indicators.note: reportedly says we want words that sound like the phrase

parts.note: Harold II fought William the Conqueror at Hastings in 1066

explanation.surface: A history lesson about the last Anglo-Saxon king's deeds, set in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, 'fought' and 'fort' are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort William is a town in the Scottish Highlands at the foot of Ben Nevis.

clue.text: Former PM, and master bridge player

parts.note: a lord is a master or ruler
North is one of the four seats at a bridge table

explanation.surface: An ex-Prime Minister who was also an expert at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link. Bridge players are named by compass points: North, South, East, West.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North was British Prime Minister 1770-1782, during the loss of the American colonies.

clue.text: Legal precedent created by playing cassette

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of cassette are played about with

explanation.surface: A court ruling set by a recording played as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like running a tape but is the anagram signal; 'created by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose outcome sets a precedent for later similar cases.

clue.text: Completely unacceptable claim

parts.note: out means not allowed, as in 'that's out'
a right is an entitlement or claim

explanation.surface: An entirely inadmissible demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely' looks like an adverb modifying 'unacceptable' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright as an adverb means totally or wholly, as in 'refused outright'.

clue.text: Left loose gown in travel bag

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a manteau is a loose gown or cloak once worn by women

explanation.surface: A baggy robe abandoned inside some luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A portmanteau is a large travelling case opening into two halves, an old-fashioned suitcase.

clue.text: Restless desires of enchantresses heading off

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter is removed

parts.note: witches are women who cast spells, enchantresses

explanation.surface: Uneasy longings belonging to sorceresses who are leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the W; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Itches are restless cravings, as in an itch to travel.

clue.text: Part of Savoy's terms for shellfish

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grand London hotel's conditions for serving seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: The oyster is a bivalve mollusc, a classic shellfish served raw on ice.

clue.text: Attempt to deceive Greek god concealing last of many

indicators.note: concealing says the god's name hides the next letter inside it

parts.note: Triton is the Greek sea god, son of Poseidon

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A scheme to fool a deity by hiding the final one of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' is the container signal; 'Attempt' looks like a noun but the definition is the verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To try it on is a British idiom for attempting to get away with something or bluff someone.

clue.text: Consumer after second wide top

indicators.note: after means the consumer comes behind the other pieces

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
an eater is one who consumes

explanation.surface: The consumer coming second, or a wide, top-class shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide is a cricket delivery bowled out of the batter's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted garment for the upper body, a kind of top.

clue.text: Outburst, the result of short report ending in criticism

indicators.note: short says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a story is a news report

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An angry flare-up caused by a brief news item that closes with censure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims STORY to STOR; 'the result of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm is a violent display of feeling, as in a storm of protest.

clue.text: See 7
Phoned some dealer angrily

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Called a seller in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rang is the past tense of ring, to telephone someone.

clue.text: Deal an effective blow, refuse to work in the house

parts.note: to strike is to refuse to work in protest
a home is a house

explanation.surface: Industrial action at home portrayed as a knockout punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike home means to land a blow squarely or have the intended impact.

clue.text: Household cat perhaps catching small mouse?

indicators.note: catching says the first word takes the next inside it

parts.note: a cat is one example of a household pet

explanation.surface: A house cat pouncing on a tiny rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mouse?' looks like the cat's prey, but the question mark marks it as an example of a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Mice are pests in a home, so a mouse is one example of a nuisance creature.
